messages.author: bc13a282f8b0c08b
messages.subject: Re: Error with 'linear' summary method
parts:
Hi,


currently, dataProcess process returns an error if summarization failed for any of the proteins. So we need to remove these proteins prior to summarization. TMP behaves differently, which is why you're getting results with one method, but not the other. TMP is a recommended strategy in MSstats, btw.

As for a solution:
Did you use a MSstats converter to process your data? If so, please try to re-run the converter with option "removeProtein_with1Feature" or "removeProtein_with1Peptide" set to TRUE and then use dataProcess again. If you didn't use a converter, please try to remove proteins for which there is only one feature.
Please also make sure that you are using the correct option for "censoredInt".

If the summarization still fails, please let me know. If it works, but you'd like to keep at least some of the proteins with a single feature, we can try to pinpoint the problem further.

Best,
Mateusz

Hi Hayley,

I think that is because of annotation for condition and bioReplicate column.
Currently, annotation is :
   Condition BioReplicate                                Run
 Condition1                   1   QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_1_3ng_270914
 Condition4                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_10_15ng_270914
 Condition4                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_11_15ng_270914
 Condition4                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_12_15ng_270914
 Condition1                   1   QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_2_3ng_270914
 Condition1                   1   QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_3_3ng_270914
 Condition2                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_4_7-5ng_270914
 Condition2                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_5_7-5ng_270914
 Condition2                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_6_7-5ng_270914
 Condition3                   1  QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_7_10ng_270914
 Condition3                   1  QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_8_10ng_270914
 Condition3                   1  QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_9_10ng_270914

Based on this information, MSstats interprets that 4 conditions come from one biological replicate, which might be paired-design.
To help MSstats recognize this design as group comparison, each condition should have different biological ID. For example, Condition1 should have BioReplicate=1, Condition2 should have BioReplicate=2, Condition3 should have BioReplicate=3 and so on.

Hope that it can help.
- Meena

Hi,


currently, dataProcess process returns an error if summarization failed for any of the proteins. So we need to remove these proteins prior to summarization. TMP behaves differently, which is why you're getting results with one method, but not the other. TMP is a recommended strategy in MSstats, btw.

As for a solution:
Did you use a MSstats converter to process your data? If so, please try to re-run the converter with option "removeProtein_with1Feature" or "removeProtein_with1Peptide" set to TRUE and then use dataProcess again. If you didn't use a converter, please try to remove proteins for which there is only one feature.
Please also make sure that you are using the correct option for "censoredInt".

If the summarization still fails, please let me know. If it works, but you'd like to keep at least some of the proteins with a single feature, we can try to pinpoint the problem further.

Best,
Mateusz
